**My reasoning as this farmer:**

I have been growing wheat and corn on this land for thirty years, same as my father before me. In Quzhou, everyone grows wheat in the winter and corn in the summer on the same plots — that is just how it works here. I have about 10 mu of farmland. I will not change what I grow. The wheat-corn rotation is what the cooperative buys, what the market wants, and what I know how to do.

For wheat, I use the improved variety from the township supply station — something like Liangxing 99, which my neighbor has used for years with good results. I am not going to experiment with something unfamiliar at my age. I plant in mid-October after the summer corn is off the land. I rotary-till first to break up the soil. For fertilizer, I put down a base of compound fertilizer before planting, then I top-dress urea at jointing stage. Water is the big worry here — we have to pump groundwater. I will irrigate before winter sets in, at jointing, and at grain filling. That is three times. I spray herbicide in spring when the weeds come up, and I spray for powdery mildew and aphids closer to heading — two or three times total with pesticides.

After I harvest wheat in June, I plant corn right away without deep plowing. Summer is short and I cannot waste time. I buy hybrid seed from the station every year — everyone does now, you cannot save corn seed. I apply fertilizer at planting and again when the corn is knee-high. If it is dry in July during pollination, I will pump water once or twice. Corn does not need as much spraying.

I will keep a small piece — half a mu — for family vegetables. That has nothing to do with money, just for eating at home.
